d.note: Family-run Main Street diner whose chili-sauced 'Texas hot' has been made by the Raptis and Rigas families since 1921.
d.fn: Opened in Wellsville in November 1921 by cousins James Rigas and George Raptis; added to the state Historic Business Preservation Registry in 2022. Sources don't say outright that it has always been at 132 N Main.

d.note: Foote Avenue hot dog shop opened by a son of Johnny's Lunch's founder (a separate Michael's AJ Texas Hots on E. Second St has closed).
d.fn: Sam Colera opened AJ Texas Hots on June 11, 1968, naming it for his father Adolph John (Post-Journal, 2018); the 2018 story pictures it at 824 Foote Ave but doesn't say it never moved.

d.note: Fourth-generation Jamestown hot dog counter whose regulars order three Texas hots 'with everything' under its secret sauce.
d.fn: Johnny Colera opened Johnny's Lunch in 1936 at Brooklyn Square; that building was razed for urban renewal in 1973 and it reopened at its current Fairmount Ave home by April 1974 (Post-Journal). The Post-Journal printed the address as 986; the 2026 National Comedy Center dining guide lists 966.

d.note: Millersport Highway bar and restaurant, a stop on the Buffalo Wing Trail.
The Main Street original of the bar that claims to be the birthplace of the Buffalo wing.
d.fn: Opened by Frank and Teressa Bellissimo in 1935 (Wikipedia); year at 1047 Main St not confirmed. The bar's own story says wings were first served here on March 4, 1964 (its claim): the Buffalo History Museum notes John Young sold wings at Wings & Things (1313 Jefferson Ave) from 1966 and that an 1857 Buffalo hotel menu listed fried chicken wings, and a 2026 archival timeline found the records don't match either pioneer's origin dates.

d.note: Family drive-in pairing roast beef on weck with egg-rich frozen custard; the family marked 80 years in business in 2026.
d.fn: The Andersons opened their first stand in the Bronx in 1946 and on Kenmore Ave in 1947; this Sheridan Drive drive-in replaced it in 1953 and still operates (Anderson's).

d.note: South Buffalo Irish pub whose wing sauces include a 'south buffalo' flavor; beef on weck is on the menu too.
d.fn: The pub says it has hosted family events on Seneca Street for over 40 years; opening year not confirmed.

d.note: Family-owned North Buffalo pizzeria serving Buffalo-style pizza with semisweet sauce and cup-and-char pepperoni, plus wings.
Worker-owned bakery and café whose bagels are rolled, boiled, dipped and baked by hand. It is known for its bagel sandwiches.
d.fn: Its site says the sourdough culture has been going since 2014. The café's opening year isn't stated.

d.note: Wehrle Drive restaurant about a mile from the Buffalo airport, one of the Roesch family's Charlie the Butcher shops serving beef on weck.
Elmwood Avenue pub with rotating taps and pennants on the walls; its 'Buffalo Combo' pairs beef on weck with five of Cole's wings.
Abbott Road pub in South Buffalo, a stop on the Buffalo Wing Trail.
Allentown pub on Allen Street, a stop on the Buffalo Wing Trail.
Old First Ward pub with its own brewery, Old First Ward Brewing, whose beers run straight to the taps; a Buffalo Wing Trail stop with beef on weck on the menu.
d.fn: Buffalo Rising (2006) says Eugene and Mary McCarthy opened the pub in 1963.

d.note: South Buffalo sit-down pizzeria with a bar, serving Buffalo-style pizza, wings and subs.
d.fn: Co-owners Dave Powers and James Bouris had run it for 23 years as of January 2016 (Buffalo Rising); a second Imperial at 1661 Main St was announced in 2023.

d.note: North Buffalo corner tavern with a traditional tavern menu that includes chicken wings and beef on weck.
d.fn: Buffalo Rising (2018) says it has been open since 1967.

d.note: West Side pizzeria on West Ferry, one of La Nova's two locations, offering specialty crusts at no charge and a long list of wing sauces; pizza-and-wings combos are a menu staple.
d.fn: Founded in Tonawanda in 1957 (WKBW); year at West Ferry not confirmed.

d.note: Small, cash-only South Buffalo tavern opened in 1981 and known for its wings; there's a back room and an attached deck.
d.fn: Established in 1981 by chef and late owner Mark Gress (the tavern's site).

d.jbf: Emerging Chef nominee 2024 (Ryan Fernandez); Best Chef: New York State nominee 2025 (Ryan Fernandez)

d.note: Tavern near the Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus, widely considered Buffalo's oldest bar; in 2026 its owner opened the back room to a lunch concept from Osteria 166's owner.
d.fn: Opened as a grocery-saloon in 1868 by German immigrant Fredrick Schrerier (Preservation Ready); widely called Buffalo's oldest bar. It closed briefly in 2012 and again from October 2013 to June 2014.

d.jbf: Outstanding Wine and Other Beverages Program semifinalist 2023; Outstanding Wine and Other Beverages Program nominee 2024; Outstanding Wine and Other Beverages Program semifinalist 2025

d.note: Pizzeria at Transit Road and Clinton Street finishing Buffalo-style pies with hand-cut cup-and-char pepperoni and Romano 'fufu dust'.
d.fn: Santora's says it opened Buffalo's first pizzeria, Santora's Pizzeria Napolitano, in 1927 (its claim); opening year of this Transit Rd shop not confirmed.

d.note: Morning bagel shop that rolls and kettle-boils its bagels and seeds them on both sides before baking. It has a second shop in Hamburg.
East Aurora village tavern on the Buffalo Wing Trail, also named by I LOVE NY for beef on weck; its owners took over the Ellicottville Depot in 2025.
Bailey Avenue takeout shop of the Bocce Club name, near UB's South Campus; its timeline says the current brick building went up in 1966.
d.fn: Bocce Club dates its pizza to 1946, when Dino Pacciotti and his sister bought a bocce club on Hickory Street; the Bailey Avenue shop opened in 1959 (its timeline).

d.note: The original Duff's, a 1946 corner tavern at Sheridan Drive and Millersport Highway that started serving wings in 1969; beef on weck is on the menu too.
d.fn: Louise Duffney opened a corner gin mill at Sheridan Dr and Millersport Hwy in 1946; first wings in 1969; Duff's says it still operates in that original location.

d.note: Hamburg village tavern on South Buffalo Street, a stop on the Buffalo Wing Trail.
Village of Hamburg shop of the Derby bagel maker, which rolls and kettle-boils its bagels before baking them. Open mornings only.
Bills-fan tavern on Abbott Road and a Buffalo Wing Trail stop; its wing list runs to dozens of sauces and dry rubs, Chiavetta's among them.
d.fn: Opened in 2010 by Rick and Peggy Cerrone (its site).

d.note: Sheridan Drive stand of Buffalo's charcoal-broiled hot dog chain, open since 1948.
d.fn: Founded in 1927 at a stand near the Peace Bridge; Ted's says its second location, on Sheridan Drive in the Town of Tonawanda, opened in 1948.

d.note: Buffalo-style pizzeria that keeps its founder's dough and sauce recipes and hand-cuts its pepperoni; this Union Road shop is one of four locations.
d.fn: Picasso's says it has served Buffalo-style pizza since 1980 and has four Western New York locations; opening year of this shop not confirmed.

d.note: Ebenezer dining room that calls itself the home of Buffalo's original roast beef on kummelweck, hand-carved and served with German potato salad and coleslaw or pickled beets.
d.fn: Schwabl's traces its name and tradition to 1837 (its claim); its history page says it has been in Ebenezer, in the Town of West Seneca, since 1942, so it is not pre-1920 at this address.

d.note: Williamsville village restaurant dating to 1827 (its claim), on a two-foot-thick limestone foundation and now run by the Hanny family; beef on weck and French onion soup are on the menu.
d.fn: The Eagle House says founder Oziel Smith opened it in 1827 (the first structure burned and he rebuilt); it claims the longest continuously held liquor license in New York State. Both are the restaurant's claims.

d.note: Village tavern with hand-hewn beams and its original mahogany bar, known for hand-carved beef on weck on a kummelweck roll and jumbo wings with a long sauce list that includes Sicilian.
d.fn: The tavern says its brick building went up in 1887, on the stagecoach route along Main Street, and has operated as a restaurant and pub ever since (its claim).
